chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, and Durust, and Hisham ibn Salim, all from Ajlan Abi Salih, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'The one who drinks an intoxicant, or gives it to a child who does not have intellect, I will quench him with scalding water as a punishment or grant him forgiveness; and the one who leaves the intoxicant seeking My pleasure, I will admit him into Paradise, quench him from the sealed nectar, and deal with him in terms of prestige as I deal with My guardians.'

key_terms.الرَّحِيقِ الْمَخْتُومِ: The sealed nectar (a specific drink of Paradise)
key_terms.مَاءِ الْحَمِيمِ: Scalding water (a form of punishment in Hell)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for abstaining from intoxicants for the sake of God according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this Hadith Qudsi emphasizes the spiritual merit of abstaining from intoxicants not merely as legal compliance but as an act of seeking divine pleasure (ibtigha' maradat Allah). It contrasts the punishment of drinking or feeding it to a child with the reward of Paradise and the 'Sealed Nectar' (Al-Raheeq Al-Makhoom) for the abstainer, highlighting the concept of divine intimacy with the righteous.
